clue.text: Revolutionary leader gripped by Vedic astrologers

indicators.note: the letters wanted are held within the run of the words Vedic astrologers, straddling the gap

explanation.surface: A political firebrand seeks guidance from Hindu stargazers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gripped by' signals letters held inside the phrase: the end of Vedic and the start of astrologers.
explanation.definitionFit: Fidel Castro led the Cuban revolution, so he is a revolutionary leader by name.

clue.text: Complaints drop off in bad weather

parts.note: minor illnesses are complaints, and colds are a common example
to drop off is to doze, i.e. take a nap

explanation.surface: Grumbles subside when the weather turns nasty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drop off' reads as 'decrease', but here it means fall asleep briefly.
explanation.definitionFit: A sudden spell of freezing temperatures is a classic example of bad weather.

clue.text: Boxing promoter in the waste business

definitions.text: Boxing promoter in the waste business

parts.words: Boxing promoter in the waste business
parts.note: a fight is a scrap, so someone who deals in fights could jokingly be a dealer in scraps; read straight, the phrase means a trader in discarded metal

explanation.surface: A fight promoter who also runs a rubbish firm.
explanation.walkthrough: The joke rests on 'scrap' meaning both a fistfight and waste metal.
explanation.definitionFit: A trader who buys and sells discarded metal and junk works in the waste business.

indicators.note: originally points to how the word Retriever begins, its opening letter

parts.note: an ace is the best at something

explanation.surface: A dog-show judge names a retriever best of breed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'best of breed' reads as a show title; 'of' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Breed and race are synonyms for a distinct lineage of animals or people.

parts.note: to black something is to boycott or ban it, as unions blacked goods
a cap is a player selected for their national team, an international

explanation.surface: A sports authority suspends a winger who plays for their country.
explanation.walkthrough: 'winger' suggests a football wide player, but it means a bird; a cap is a British term for a player picked for the national side.
explanation.definitionFit: Anything with wings can be a winger; the blackcap is a small warbler, a bird.

clue.text: Girl embraces star in US resort

indicators.note: embraces means the girl word wraps around the star word

parts.note: lass is a Scottish and northern English word for girl
Vega is the brightest star in the constellation Lyra

explanation.surface: A young woman hugs a celebrity at an American holiday spot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'star' suggests a celebrity, but it is the astronomical star Vega.
explanation.definitionFit: The Nevada city of casinos and shows is a famous American resort destination.

parts.note: Com. is a dictionary abbreviation for commander
a parable is a simple story told to teach a moral

explanation.surface: An officer is fond of telling instructive stories.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Like' looks like a verb, but it is the adjective 'similar'.
explanation.definitionFit: Like and comparable both describe things similar enough to be set side by side.

indicators.note: after places the runs letter behind the copper symbol

parts.note: Cu is the chemical symbol for copper
R is the cricket scoring abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: A villain flees after a police officer appears.
explanation.walkthrough: 'copper' suggests a policeman, but it is the metal.
explanation.definitionFit: Cur is an old insult for a contemptible man, a synonym of scoundrel.

indicators.note: consumed by means the energy letter is swallowed inside the factory word

parts.note: a plant is an industrial works or factory
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: The globe's power is used up by industry.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's of 'World's' stands for 'is', a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A planet is a world, such as Earth or Mars, orbiting a star.

indicators.note: in places the left letter inside the agony word

parts.note: agony is extreme pain

explanation.surface: Someone abandoned in torment exclaims that it's obvious.
explanation.definitionFit: Plain and evident both mean clear to see or understand.

clue.text: Car Lily wrecked is carried away

indicators.note: a wrecked thing is smashed apart, so the letters of these two words are rearranged

explanation.surface: Lily crashed the car and was taken off in an ambulance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'carried away' reads as being taken away injured but means effusive or rhapsodic.
explanation.definitionFit: To wax lyrical is to be effusively enthusiastic, as someone carried away by feeling.

clue.text: Man has song from old Israeli capital

parts.note: Sam is a man's name
an aria is a solo song in an opera

explanation.surface: A man sings a song from an ancient city.
explanation.definitionFit: Samaria was the capital of the northern kingdom of Israel in biblical times.

clue.text: Concessions for son having surgical procedures

parts.note: S is the genealogical abbreviation for son
ops is short for operations, surgical procedures

explanation.surface: A boy undergoing surgery is given special allowances.
explanation.definitionFit: A sop is a small concession offered to placate someone.

clue.text: Teams become confused when not sitting up straight

parts.note: sides are opposing teams in a game
to addle is to muddle, or become muddled

explanation.surface: Teams get muddled when the players slouch.
explanation.walkthrough: A rider sitting sidesaddle has both legs on one side of the horse rather than astride it.
explanation.definitionFit: Riding with both legs to one side means sitting sideways, not upright astride the mount.

indicators.note: curiously means in an odd way, so the letters of considerate are put in an odd order

explanation.surface: Oddly thoughtful behaviour towards places of worship.
explanation.definitionFit: Desecration is the violation of a sacred place or object, a sacrilegious vandalism.

clue.text: Cat kept by defendant at home

indicators.note: kept by means the cat word is held inside the defendant word

parts.note: the accused is the defendant in a criminal trial
a tom is a male cat

explanation.surface: A pet cat is looked after at home by someone awaiting trial.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at home' reads as a location but means familiar or used to something.
explanation.definitionFit: Being at home with something means being used to it, familiar through habit.

definitions.meaning: means as a noun: the instrument or medium by which something is done
a business such as a travel or advertising firm

explanation.surface: Someone stresses that they are serious about it.
explanation.definitionFit: The word covers both a medium of action and a firm providing a service.

clue.text: Discomfort from a meal is dreadful

indicators.note: dreadful suggests something in a terrible state, so the letters of a meal is are jumbled

explanation.surface: Indigestion after a terrible dinner.
explanation.definitionFit: Malaise is a general feeling of unease or bodily discomfort.

parts.note: a reef is a ridge or bank of rock or sand near the water surface
the knot is a wading bird

explanation.surface: A riverbank where a bird got caught up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' is a link here, and the 's of 'bird's' marks the next piece's ownership.
explanation.definitionFit: A reef knot is a tie, so a deliberate tangle of rope, i.e. an entanglement.

clue.text: A call for help, being without optimal fire retardant

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so A and the distress call stand outside the optimal word

parts.note: SOS is the international distress signal
optimal means best

explanation.surface: Someone shouts for help without the ideal fireproofing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'being without' reads as 'lacking', but 'without' is used in its old sense of 'outside', so the outer pieces surround the optimal word.
explanation.definitionFit: This fibrous mineral was widely used to resist fire before its health risks were known.

indicators.note: arresting means the federal agent word holds the yob word inside it

parts.note: a G-man is an FBI agent, a Fed
a yob is a British word for a lout or hooligan

explanation.surface: An FBI agent ignored orders while detaining a thug.
explanation.definitionFit: To flout a rule is to openly ignore it, so flouted means disregarded.

parts.note: bob was slang for a shilling in pre-decimal British money, abbreviated s
to lack something is to have none of it

explanation.surface: An elderly man called Bob goes without his trousers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bob' looks like a name; a bob was an old British shilling, written s.
explanation.definitionFit: Slacks are casual trousers, so the plural matches.

parts.note: of can mean from, as in a man of Kent
a fair is a trade show or exhibition

explanation.surface: A TV report is not being aired from the trade show.
explanation.definitionFit: A station that is silent and not transmitting is described as being off the air.

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for 100, many
lean means thin or slim

explanation.surface: Lots of people get thin by doing weight training.
explanation.walkthrough: In weightlifting the clean is the move raising the bar to the shoulders, as in clean and jerk.
explanation.definitionFit: Weightlifters perform this specific lift, hoisting the barbell from floor to shoulder.

clue.text: Trees to come down before anything else

parts.note: firs are coniferous trees
to fall is to come down

explanation.surface: The trees must be felled before any other job.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means initially, as the very first priority ahead of everything.

parts.note: B is the chess abbreviation for bishop
a tipple is an alcoholic drink, such as ale

explanation.surface: A clergyman's supply of drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pack' reads as a quantity of drink, but it is the definition: a bundle.
explanation.definitionFit: A bale is a large tied bundle of goods such as hay or cotton, a pack.

definitions.meaning: to discard or cast off, as a snake its skin
a small hut or outbuilding in a garden

explanation.surface: Someone decides to clear away a garden building.
explanation.definitionFit: One word serves as both a verb for discarding and a noun for a simple hut.

parts.note: an album is a blank book for photos or stamps
in can mean involved or concerned with, as in in politics

explanation.surface: A volume about dietary nutrients.
explanation.definitionFit: Albumin is a water-soluble protein found in egg white and blood plasma.

parts.note: hum is British slang for a bad smell, BO being body odour
p is the musical notation piano, softly

explanation.surface: Someone murmurs a tune quietly while dancing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hum' reads as singing with closed lips, but here it is the British slang for a smell.
explanation.definitionFit: To bop is to dance to pop music in an informal way.

parts.note: at can mean busy or engaged in, as in at work
a heist is a robbery, often armed

explanation.surface: A doubter turns out to be involved in a hold-up.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who doubts that any god exists is a religious sceptic.

clue.text: Speed with which pair tidy mess

indicators.note: mess as a verb means to throw into disorder, so the letters of pair tidy are scrambled

explanation.surface: The quickness with which two people clean up a mess.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mess' reads as a noun the pair tidy, but it acts as the verb muddling their letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Rapidity is quickness, so it is a synonym of speed.

clue.text: Handsome youth rejected wickedness after trouble

indicators.note: after puts the wickedness piece behind the trouble word

parts.note: ado is fuss or trouble

indicators.note: rejected means turned back, so the wickedness word is read in reverse

parts.note: sin is wickedness

explanation.surface: A good-looking young man turned away from vice after a scrape.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rejected' is the reversal signal, read as turned back; 'after' sets the order of the two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth this beautiful young man was loved by Aphrodite, so his name means a handsome youth.
